about: Engine and live conformance cases for the HTML cache (Markdown alternate).
This file is module-only. Policy verdicts are proven by the optimizer's shared
policy cases, which this file never repeats; rows here assert what the engine
passes to the library and does with its verdicts (engine) and what each server
port sends (live). Adapter and engine changes add rows here.
ROWS. Each row has: id (unique, [a-z0-9-]), runners (one or both of engine,
live; never policy), why (a public label: an RFC section or a short rule
name), optional ports (subset of apache, nginx, iis; absent = all), and one
body per runner it names. A row whose knob a port reads differently is written
once per port with its own ports list, never as a verdict override.
engine body: config (overrides of mode, agent_optimize, max_bytes,
host_names, budget_bytes, sites), library (overrides of minor, set_bound,
html_mode, agent_entitled for the fake library), volume (entries present
before the first step: kind original | sidecar | markdown | withheld | epoch),
verdicts (results the fake library returns, consumed in order per fn; a
store verdict may carry the reason detail, such as request for a request
no-store), and
steps. A step has kind (capture | serve | poll_tick | stats_tick |
admin_purge), optional pre (ops run before it), request, response (capture:
status, origin, store_delta, final_delta, module, body_ref, aborted), during
(capture only: [{point before_send | after_send | after_commit |
after_recheck, do: [ops]}]; before_send is after capture_start and before the
origin request goes out)
and expect. pre and do ops are one-key objects: purge_url, purge_global,
flush_file, wipe_file_cache, create_engine, advance_clock, make_visible,
disable_recheck, budget. expect keys: calls (an ordered subsequence of the
library calls made in the step: other calls may come between, and each
listed call is matched on the subset of arguments given; dotted names
address struct fields; a call's exact [request | stored] makes the match
fail when the call carried a field of that struct the args do not name, so
the row states the whole struct: every flag bit, flags_unknown for any bit
without a name, and a hash as zero or sha256:<body>), calls_exclude (fns
never called in the step),
port_calls and port_calls_exclude (port methods called or never called),
stored, removed,
notify ([] = none), counters (deltas), serve {kind fall_through | final,
status, reason, headers_exact (the complete header set the port is asked to
emit: no other line), body_bytes}, log_lines, admin_response,
purge_set_added, volume_epoch_s, budget_in_use. An absent key is not
asserted. A volume original with paired true has a stamp equal to the
pairing hash of the volume's sidecar entry for the same url; with no sidecar
entry it needs no header block. A header value $len:<body> is the byte
length of that entry of bodies.
live body: mode, agent_optimize, vhost (knobs: header_add, header_always,
header_early, expires, auth, alias, default_vhost, in_place,
pagespeed_off_location, compress_markdown, third_party_filter, merge_slashes, gunzip,
poll_interval_s, respect_xfp, chained_module_origin), origin {status, headers, body_ref,
echo_conditionals, truncate_body (the body ends before its Content-Length)},
and steps [{request {method, path, host, headers}, pre,
process, background, window, expect}]. live pre ops: purge_url {url, form PURGE |
query}, purge_global {via admin | flush_file}, wait_markdown {timeout_s,
expect_ready (default true; false = the copy must NOT become servable
within the timeout)}, sleep_s,
origin_set, hold_origin, release_origin, set_mode, wait_origin_held {method,
path, timeout_s} (the held origin response for that request has its
headers out and waits; a step that releases the origin must wait for it
first, before any purge in its pre ops), wait_coded {codings (br, gzip),
timeout_s} (the volume holds those coded copies of the request URL's
Markdown copy), restart_worker {gzip_level, brotli_level} (the optimizer
worker restarted on the same volume with these levels and the server
reloaded; the provider restores the defaults after the row). live expect
keys: status,
content_type, headers_exact (name -> {count, value | contains | tokens: the
comma-separated list in order, names case-insensitive, spaces ignored}),
headers_only (no header beyond headers_exact and the server core's
transport lines Date, Server, Connection, Keep-Alive, Transfer-Encoding),
headers_absent, stored (an original entry for the request URL is present
in the volume after the step, read by exact id), stored_lifetime_s,
sidecar_absent, body_ref,
body_bytes, body_contains (strings the body must hold),
length_matches_body, decoded_equals_step (the body decoded by its one
Content-Encoding, none, gzip or br, equals an earlier step's body, by
index), header_equals_step ({name: index}: the lines equal that step's),
origin_saw, origin_saw_absent,
counter_delta, differential {against: modes, allow_vary_accept}. The request
header value $markdown_etag is replaced by the ETag of the last Markdown 200.
counter_delta spans the whole step, its pre ops included. allow_vary_accept
requires the one Accept token it allows. A background step is checked after
the next step ran and asserts only its own response (status, content_type,
headers_*, body_*, length_matches_body). Volume, counter and origin reads
come after the provider settled every commit of answered requests.
A window step {stale_max_s, margin_s, observe_s, every_s, stale
{content_type}} watches its process across the purge in its pre ops: it
sends its request every every_s until observe_s after the purge returned.
A response with the stale content type (the pre-purge entry) is allowed
only for a request sent within stale_max_s (the server's poll interval)
plus margin_s of the purge, and never after a response without it; every
other response meets expect (response keys only). margin_s 2 covers the
whole-second poll clock (a process checks once the second count reaches
its last check plus the interval) and the spacing of the requests.
A row whose steps name processes is checked after its last step: each
named process was one server process, no two names were the same one,
and the purges of a window step were answered by a process other than
the one it watches.
The window rows keep the origin body unchanged across the purge: a new
body unbinds the old Markdown copy by itself and would hide a process
that never saw the purge.
bodies: fixture bodies referenced by body_ref.
PENDING ROWS. A row may carry pending (the one value serve-cached-html): it
describes the cached-HTML serve path before its engine and runner support
exist. Both runners skip pending rows and count them apart from the zero-skip
count; the shape check still checks them. The engine runner reads every
engine key and value marked (serve-cached-html) below, so any engine row may
use them; it runs each pending engine row to its end in a check of its own,
which fails when the row uses a key the runner does not read, or when the
row already passes (its marker must then go). Only a pending row may use a
live key or value marked (serve-cached-html). The change that adds the
support removes the markers.
(serve-cached-html) engine body: config adds serve_scope (agents | all),
max_age_s (absent = the default cap, 3600), credentialed (anonymous-only |
explicit-public), ignore_cookies, ignore_cookie (list), policy_stamp (the
vhost stamp the fake's ps_html_policy_stamp returns; absent =
5a17c0de00000001), and the mode serve-cached-html; library adds missing
(1.15 symbols left unbound). A row whose config names any of these settings
or that mode states its library minor (14 or 15); a row without a minor
runs on minor 14. Volume original adds
content_type, store_v2 and anonymous_recorded; sidecar adds format (3) and
policy_stamp, the ONE source
of an entry's stamp (absent = none). DEFAULTS: an original without store_v2
or anonymous_recorded has both set (the earlier rows describe such entries);
every serve-cached-html row states them. A store verdict's flags are exactly
the ones it lists (absent = none, so request_anonymous is clear). Request adds
agent_class (0 to 3; absent = classified from user_agent), user_agent,
signature (signed_agent | verified_bot | not_ready | failed),
internal_redirect, internal, served_from_cache, cookie_lines,
proxy_authorization, request_headers ([name, value]; merged with headers
into one list, and a header name given under both is a row error), raw_path,
if_match, if_unmodified_since. Step kinds add unsafe (request, response
{status, location and content_location, each a line or a list of lines}),
unsafe_many (count requests to distinct targets, the request path with -<n>
appended), emit_fails (a serve whose EmitAsOrigin returns false),
begin_recording and configure; a capture response adds split_at (its chunk
boundary); a step may carry repeat (the
same request that many times; counters are the deltas over all of them). Ops
add disable_credential_skip (a _for_testing setter on the engine that no
directive, option or environment variable reaches and product code never
calls: it turns off the request-credential skip before any read, so an
emit-time refusal is reachable; only rows whose request carries a
credential use it) and, inside during, unsafe {method, status, url}.
Verdicts add ps_html_classify_cookies {class, first_blocking,
ignorable_values, ignorable_count (the count reported, when more than the
values listed)}, ps_html_request_guard {reason, header_index, xfp},
ps_html_ignore_cookie_guard {accepted, warning}, ps_html_policy_stamp
{value} and ps_html_unsafe_method_invalidates
{value}; ps_cache_remove_site rc may name not_found or io. Expect adds serve
kind as_origin with body_ref, header_order and suppress_recording;
headers_absent, classify_calls (ps_html_serve_classify calls in the step),
decision_lines {contains, absent}, recording_started, config_error
({contains} or null), fence_before_remove, removed_count,
fence_map_size_max, fences_kept, oldest_fenced, newest_fenced, agent_class,
classify_agent_calls and agent_vectors (every line of that vector file);
volume_epoch_s null means the epoch was never written; removed may list
urls; a stored entry may say its kind (original).
Counter names are the engine's.
(serve-cached-html) live body: origin may be {app adversarial, kind static |
cgi | proxy}: test/system/daemon_html/adversarial_origin.py (and its static
pages) behind the server, request paths naming its endpoints. Vhost knobs
add serve_scope, max_age_s, credentialed, ignore_cookies, expires_by_type,
deflate, ssi, substitute, proxy_html, sub_filter, rewriter_off_for_type,
rewriter_declines, disable_rewrite_on_no_transform, tls_front,
redirect. Ops add set_vhost {knob: value}, protect {variant}, origin_fail
{path, status}, fill_read_queue, release_slow {sticky}. Step keys add
abort_after_ms. Expect adds body_cred_identity (the identity whose credential
hash the body carries), log_count {contains, count} (over the whole row),
origin_requests_delta (requests the origin answered during the step), hit,
status_in, age_at_least, rewriter_visible, body_equals_miss, body_contains,
header_multiset_equals_miss and expires_equals_storing_miss (the hit-vs-miss
rule), log_contains, client_aborted, hit_vs_miss {pairs, max_spans,
max_span_bytes} (the differential with a bounded learned mask),
token_binding {paths, identities, credentialed, anonymous_class, allowed}
and hit_stops_within_s. token_binding runs every pair: this identity stores,
that one requests. A hit body must carry the requester's own credential
hash, except between two identities of anonymous_class (no cookie, or only
ignored cookies, and no authorization: the cache cannot tell them apart)
and in an allowed cell (a labelled operator opt-in); any other share fails.
Reasons are the library's (cookie_request, auth_request, cookie_echo, ...);
An unsafe request whose URL the server and the module read differently
removes nothing: no key mapping is guessed, and the stored page stays
bounded by the cap (a documented residual).
a decision line carries a cookie or header name in detail, never a value.
